propositions: A contributor can post a `recheck-review` magic comment on a change with a current-revision LLM-Review -1 to trigger a fresh review, provided the -1 is not a real finding BLOCK.

The eligibility precheck reads the bot's current-revision message tag from Gerrit (durable privileged state), refuses only `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` and its merge variant, and accepts all coverage-gap sub-reasons and escalated states.

On acceptance, the retrigger resets the per-revision retry budget via `dedup.reset_attempts()` and enqueues a forced re-review (bypassing dedup/existing-vote short-circuits); on refusal, it posts a reply comment with no vote.
The reply path uses `gerrit_client.post_comment()` with a message-only JSON body (no `labels` key) to ensure no direct label writes occur.
Bot-authored comments and comments lacking the `recheck-review` token are silent no-ops; `/rerun` also resets the budget to harmonize semantics with the contributor trigger.

The tag parser must handle all three production forms: `_TAG_SUFFIXES` members, the hardcoded `merge-review` literal, and in-tag `(merge-change, …)` suffixes, with fail-open behavior for unparseable tags.
